items.title: Clearance Warehouse Opens Oakville Location Just West of the Mississauga Border
items.summary: A new discount retailer has opened just outside Mississauga, giving bargain hunters another option for deals on household goods and name-brand merchandise. According to insauga.com, Clearance Warehouse opened its newest location on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 2307 Royal Windsor Drive in Oakville, in a roughly 30,000-square-foot space that previously housed a RONA store just west of the Mississauga border. The store is stocked with liquidation, overstock and clearance merchandise advertised at discounts of 30 to 90 per cent off regular retail prices, including housewares, small appliances, bedding, health and beauty products and tools. The selection is expected to change regularly as new stock arrives and existing inventory sells through. The Oakville store joins existing Clearance Warehouse locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, both of which opened for the current sale period in October, with all three locations running their sales until Dec. 24.

items.title: Mississauga Targets 4,100-Tonne Cut to Winter Road Salt Use
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it plans to significantly reduce how much road salt it uses this winter, aiming to protect the environment and infrastructure while keeping roads safe for drivers. According to city officials, the expanded salt-reduction effort is expected to cut road salt use by as much as 4,100 tonnes a year. The city said it will extend anti-icing brine, a liquid mix of water and salt, to 20 per cent more roads in 2026, a change expected to reduce salt use by up to 650 tonnes annually. Officials said they will also begin plowing snow earlier on select major roads, a step they estimate could cut salt use by a further 3,450 tonnes a year. The brine program currently covers about 1,260 lane kilometres of roadway, using roughly 63,000 litres of salt brine for each application, city officials said.

items.title: Food Basics to Replace Decades-Old Metro Store at Lakeshore Plaza
items.summary: A Mississauga grocery store with a history stretching back decades has closed, according to insauga.com, marking the end of an era for a Lakeview neighbourhood shopping plaza. The Metro location at 406 Lakeshore Road East, in the Lakeshore Plaza near Cawthra Road, shut its doors on Nov. 4 after operating over the years under several different banners, including Miracle Food Mart and Dominion before becoming Metro. The site reported the space is being converted into a Food Basics store, with the discount grocery banner expected to open sometime in the new year. The parent company has been converting a number of its traditional Metro locations into Food Basics stores as shoppers increasingly look for ways to save on groceries, insauga.com said. The Lakeshore Plaza location will remain under the same corporate ownership even as its shopping format changes.

items.title: Minto Completes First-Ever Seniors-to-Rental Conversion at Former Chartwell Site in Meadowvale
items.summary: Real estate company Minto has finished converting a pair of former seniors' apartment buildings in Mississauga's Meadowvale neighbourhood into a rental community, more than two years after a controversial mass eviction at the site. According to insauga.com, the two 10-storey towers at 6509 and 6521 Glen Erin Dr. were previously known as the Chartwell Heritage Glen Retirement Residence before Minto purchased the property in early 2024. Chartwell served roughly 188 eviction notices and required seniors to leave by July 2024, saying at the time that the buildings' aging infrastructure made continuing to operate as a retirement residence unsustainable. A Minto representative named Tovey said only one former resident chose to return and rent a unit once the renovation was complete. Tovey said the project, finished under budget and ahead of schedule, marks the first seniors-to-rental conversion Minto has completed.

items.title: Peel Health Issues Conditional Passes to New Supermarket, Three Mississauga Restaurants
items.summary: Peel Public Health issued conditional passes to a newly opened Mississauga supermarket and three restaurants following recent inspections, according to Mississauga.com. The outlet reported that Food World Plus, the large grocery store at 50 Matheson Blvd., received conditional passes for two of its sections, the deli and the food square area, while Fuwa Fuwa Japanese Pancakes, Pure Punjabi Sweets & Restaurant and Lazeez Shawarma also received conditional passes. Mississauga.com said follow-up inspections at all four businesses later resulted in full passes. The inspection program is designed to give the public information about the health and safety compliance of local food establishments, the outlet said, with inspectors routinely checking restaurants, bakeries, takeout spots and other food-serving businesses. Mississauga.com noted the article was updated on Nov. 6 to reflect the passing results of those follow-up inspections.

items.title: Streetsville's Hyde Mill Ruins to Be Preserved as Three Unsafe Structures Come Down
items.summary: Three deteriorating structures at Mississauga's Hyde Mill Ruins are being torn down over safety concerns, the city says, as crews prepare to restore the historic Streetsville site. According to Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt, the demolition targets buildings on the site, which sits on the banks of the Credit River at the foot of Ontario Street and dates back to the early 1840s, while the ruins themselves will be protected during construction and preserved in place. Butt said demolition and initial site restoration work took place in September and October. Planting and seeding are scheduled to begin next week, followed by backfilling and further landscape restoration, he said. The councillor added that temporary construction and demolition noise will continue in the area over the coming weeks.

items.title: Mississauga Reminds Residents of New Fireworks Bylaw as Diwali Celebrations Begin
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is reminding residents to follow its newer fireworks bylaw as Diwali celebrations run from Nov. 6 to 10, with the main day falling on Sunday, Nov. 8. According to the city, family and backyard fireworks can be set off without a permit on private property only on Nov. 8, while a permit is required to use them on any other day or to hold a display in a city park or other public space. Officials said fireworks are never allowed on roads, sidewalks, in parking lots or elsewhere on public property. The city said it is adding extra bylaw enforcement officers this year after receiving a record 432 complaints about Diwali fireworks during the 2025 festival. Residents were also reminded not to call 911 over fireworks unless there is immediate danger, such as a fire or injury, and to instead report illegal fireworks through the city's 311 line or website.

items.title: Jackknifed Truck Shuts Down All Express Lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga
items.summary: All express lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga were shut down Friday morning after a crash involving a jackknifed truck, according to the Ministry of Transportation's 511 traffic site. The Ontario Provincial Police confirmed the express lanes were closed while crews responded to the scene. Ministry of Transportation photos showed the jackknifed truck surrounded by emergency vehicles as crews worked to clear the wreckage. Police advised drivers to expect delays if travelling through the area and urged them to plan alternate routes where possible. Traffic backed up significantly in the express lanes as the cleanup continued into the morning.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows 332 Vehicles Stolen in Mississauga Over Two Months, Clustered Near Square One and Pearson
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows 332 vehicles were reported stolen in Mississauga between Sept. 1 and Oct. 31, averaging more than six thefts a day across the two-month span. According to the force's online crime-mapping tool, the thefts were not evenly spread across the city, with notable clusters forming around Square One and Pearson International Airport. The interactive map, available on the Peel Regional Police website, plots the approximate location of each reported theft. Police noted that some points on the map may represent more than one vehicle stolen in the same area. The tool allows residents to see where auto thefts have been concentrated in recent months across the region.
